standard_prerequisites.use: Produces an element integral over the local subring, which is what allows the extension to be kept finite.

core_obligations: Take an element x of K outside A and consider the ring obtained by adjoining the inverse of x; analyse whether the extension is transcendental or algebraic (proof lines 12153-12165).

In the algebraic case pass to a suitable integral multiple so that the resulting extension is finite and localise at a prime lying over the maximal ideal of A, producing a strictly larger local subring that dominates A (proof lines 12165-12176).
proof_roadmap: Enlarge the local subring by adjoining a controlled element (proof lines 12153-12165).
Localise to keep the extension local and dominating (proof lines 12165-12177).
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces, for an element x of the fraction field outside a local subring A, a local subring strictly containing A inside the same field and dominating it (statement lines 12140-12151). The proof does not quote a general extension theorem: it adjoins the inverse of x, splits into the transcendental and algebraic cases, in the latter replaces x by an integral multiple so that the extension is finite, and then localises at a suitable prime to keep the ring local and dominating (proof lines 12153-12177). Choosing the integral multiple so that finiteness holds is the step carrying the argument. H2.
